q: The accounts of the Government of India are kept in three parts. Which one of the following is NOT one of those parts?

options.A: Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: Contingency Fund of India
options.C: Public Account of India
options.D: Railway Reserve Fund

e: Government accounts of India are maintained in three parts only: the Consolidated Fund, the Contingency Fund and the Public Account. A Railway Reserve Fund is not one of these parts, so it is the odd one out.

q: In the audit objection process on Railways, the correct sequence is:

options.A: Audit Para, Provisional Para, Draft Para
options.B: Draft Para, Provisional Para, Audit Para
options.C: Provisional Para, Draft Para, Audit Para
options.D: Draft Para, Audit Para, Provisional Para

e: An audit objection first appears as a Draft Para, is then taken up as a Provisional Para, and finally, if included in the Report of the CAG, becomes an Audit Para. Hence the sequence is Draft Para, Provisional Para, Audit Para.

q: 'Internal check' in an Accounts office primarily means:

options.A: Inspection of the office by the audit party once a year
options.B: A system under which the work of one staff is automatically checked by another in the ordinary course of work
options.C: Check exercised by the C&AG over the accounts of Railways
options.D: Verification of cash balance by the cashier daily

e: Internal check is an arrangement within the office under which the work of one person is automatically checked by another in the ordinary course of work, without any separate inspection or outside audit.

q: Operating Ratio of a Railway is worked out as:

options.A: Net earnings divided by capital-at-charge, multiplied by 100
options.B: Working expenses divided by gross traffic earnings, multiplied by 100
options.C: Gross earnings divided by working expenses, multiplied by 100
options.D: Working expenses divided by capital-at-charge, multiplied by 100

e: Operating Ratio = Working expenses / Gross traffic earnings x 100. It shows what proportion of every rupee of earnings is absorbed by the cost of working the railway.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Charged expenditure is not submitted to the vote of Parliament.
2. Charged expenditure cannot be discussed in Parliament.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: charged expenditure is not submitted to the vote of Parliament. Statement 2 is false: charged expenditure can still be discussed in Parliament; only voting on it is barred.

q: The Appropriation Accounts of Railways are examined in detail by:

options.A: Estimates Committee
options.B: Railway Convention Committee
options.C: Public Accounts Committee
options.D: Committee on Public Undertakings

e: The Public Accounts Committee examines the Appropriation Accounts in detail to see that the moneys voted by Parliament were spent within the scope of the grants and appropriations.

q: Expenditure incurred without the sanction of the competent authority is termed as:

options.A: Excess over grant
options.B: Unnecessary expenditure
options.C: Unsanctioned expenditure
options.D: Irregular appropriation

e: Expenditure incurred without the sanction of the competent authority is termed unsanctioned expenditure, and it is reported as such until regularised by competent sanction.

q: The statutory audit of Indian Railways is conducted on behalf of:

options.A: Railway Board
options.B: Ministry of Finance
options.C: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: NITI Aayog

e: The statutory audit of Indian Railways is conducted by the Indian Audit and Accounts Department working under the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, the constitutional audit authority.

q: Appropriation Accounts are prepared to show:

options.A: The profit and loss of the Railway undertaking for the year
options.B: The comparison of actual expenditure with the grants and appropriations sanctioned by Parliament
options.C: The balance sheet of assets and liabilities of Railways
options.D: The arrears of earnings outstanding at stations

e: Appropriation Accounts compare the actual expenditure of the year with the grants voted and the appropriations sanctioned by Parliament, and explain the variations between them.

q: Which committee periodically reviews the rate of dividend/return payable by Railways to General Finances?

options.A: Railway Convention Committee
options.B: Estimates Committee
options.C: Public Accounts Committee
options.D: Standing Finance Committee

e: The Railway Convention Committee, constituted by Parliament from time to time, periodically reviews the rate of dividend or return payable by Railways to General Finances.

q: 'Link heads' in railway accounts serve the purpose of:

options.A: Connecting the Government accounts with the Commercial (Railway) accounts
options.B: Linking the accounts of one zonal railway with another
options.C: Linking the budget with the Appropriation Accounts
options.D: Connecting station accounts with the Traffic Accounts Office

e: Link heads are the connecting heads through which transactions recorded in the commercial accounts of Railways are linked with the corresponding heads in the Government accounts of the Union.

q: 'Strategic lines' on Indian Railways are lines which are:

options.A: Operated exclusively for goods traffic
options.B: Leased to private operators
options.C: Maintained primarily for strategic (defence) considerations, irrespective of commercial return
options.D: Worked by the State Governments

e: Strategic lines are railway lines maintained primarily for strategic or defence considerations, irrespective of whether they are commercially remunerative.

q: A recognised limitation of the Operating Ratio, which led to the evolution of the Performance Efficiency Index, is that the Operating Ratio:

options.A: Cannot be computed from the published accounts
options.B: Includes the dividend payable to General Finances
options.C: Is expressed in absolute figures and not as a percentage
options.D: Does not take into account differences in the composition of traffic between different railways

e: The Operating Ratio ignores differences in the composition of traffic, such as the mix of passenger and goods traffic, between different railways, so it cannot fairly compare their performance; the Performance Efficiency Index was evolved to overcome this defect.

q: A zonal railway has gross traffic earnings of Rs 2,000 crore, working expenses of Rs 1,860 crore and dividend payable of Rs 100 crore. The surplus of the railway is:

options.A: Rs 140 crore
options.B: Rs 240 crore
options.C: Rs 40 crore
options.D: Nil

e: Surplus = Gross traffic earnings - Working expenses - Dividend = Rs 2,000 crore - Rs 1,860 crore - Rs 100 crore = Rs 40 crore.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Suspense account balances are reviewed half-yearly.
2. The review of suspense balances includes examination of old outstanding items.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: suspense account balances are reviewed half-yearly, and the review specifically covers old outstanding items so that they are investigated and cleared promptly.

q: A suspense head in Government/Railway accounts is operated when:

options.A: The expenditure exceeds the budget grant
options.B: A transaction cannot, for the time being, be booked finally to its proper head of account
options.C: The accounts of the year are closed
options.D: A new service is introduced

e: A suspense head is operated when a transaction cannot, for the time being, be finally booked to its proper head of account; it is held under suspense only until correct final classification becomes possible.

q: Which of the following correctly brings out the distinction between internal check and internal audit?

options.A: Internal check is exercised by the C&AG, while internal audit is exercised by the Railway Board
options.B: Internal audit is done before a transaction and internal check after it
options.C: Internal check is built into the process of work itself, while internal audit is a subsequent review by staff not involved in the routine processing
options.D: There is no difference between the two

e: Internal check is built into the process of work itself, each step checking the previous one, whereas internal audit is a subsequent review carried out by staff not involved in the routine processing of the transactions.

q: Performance audit, as conducted by the C&AG, is mainly concerned with examining:

options.A: Whether vouchers are properly filed
options.B: The economy, efficiency and effectiveness of an organisation's operations
options.C: Whether the cash book is balanced daily
options.D: The correctness of pay fixations only

e: Performance audit examines the economy, efficiency and effectiveness, the three Es, with which an organisation has used its resources and carried out its operations.

q: A 'theme-based audit' means audit conducted:

options.A: Only of the headquarters office of a railway
options.B: Only through computerised systems
options.C: Of all transactions of one selected month
options.D: On a selected theme or subject, simultaneously across a number of field units

e: In a theme-based audit, one selected theme or subject is audited simultaneously across a number of field units, so that the findings give an overall picture of that area of working.

q: Cut motions are moved in Parliament at the stage of:

options.A: Examination of the Appropriation Accounts
options.B: Discussion and voting on the Demands for Grants
options.C: Presentation of the Report of the C&AG
options.D: Introduction of the Finance Bill only

e: Cut motions are moved when the Demands for Grants are taken up for discussion and voting in the Lok Sabha, to disapprove a policy, demand economy or ventilate a grievance.

q: The Estimates Committee of Parliament examines the estimates with a view to suggesting, among other things:

options.A: Economies and improvements in organisation and efficiency, consistent with the policy underlying the estimates
options.B: The rate of dividend payable by Railways
options.C: The quantum of bonus for railway staff
options.D: The fare and freight structure

e: The Estimates Committee examines the estimates and suggests economies, improvements in organisation and efficiency and changes in the form of presentation, consistent with the policy underlying the estimates.

q: The Appropriation Act passed by Parliament:

options.A: Compares actual expenditure with the grants
options.B: Authorises the withdrawal of moneys from the Consolidated Fund of India to meet the voted grants and charged expenditure
options.C: Fixes the salaries of railway officers
options.D: Presents the Report of the C&AG to Parliament

e: The Appropriation Act authorises the withdrawal of moneys out of the Consolidated Fund of India to meet the grants voted by the Lok Sabha and the expenditure charged on the Fund.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Government accounts are generally maintained on the cash basis.
2. Commercial accounting is based on the accrual concept.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: Government accounts are maintained generally on the cash basis, recording transactions when cash is actually received or paid, while commercial accounting is based on the accrual concept.

q: The Railway Budget was merged with the General Budget with effect from the Budget for:
e: The separate Railway Budget was merged with the General Budget, and railway finances were presented as part of the Union Budget for the first time in the Budget for 2017-18.

q: In Indian Railways, EBR(IF) refers to:

options.A: A fund created out of revenue for staff welfare
options.B: Extra Budgetary Resources raised through institutional finance (market borrowings) for financing projects
options.C: The balance of earnings retained at stations
options.D: A reserve for meeting accident compensation claims

e: EBR(IF) means Extra Budgetary Resources raised through institutional finance, that is market borrowings raised through bodies like IRFC, for financing railway projects outside the Budget.

q: Expenditure already incurred without sanction (unsanctioned expenditure) is regularised by:

options.A: Writing it off automatically at the end of the year
options.B: Obtaining the sanction of the competent authority after the expenditure has been incurred (ex-post-facto sanction)
options.C: Charging it to a suspense head permanently
options.D: Presenting a token demand in the next budget

e: Expenditure already incurred without sanction is regularised by obtaining the sanction of the competent authority after the expenditure has been incurred, that is ex-post-facto sanction; it is not written off automatically.

q: The commercial accounts maintained by Indian Railways include the preparation of:

options.A: Only the Cash Book and the General Ledger
options.B: A Profit and Loss Account and a Balance Sheet
options.C: Only the Appropriation Accounts
options.D: Only monthly Account Currents

e: Railways maintain commercial accounts on the accrual basis, which include the preparation of a Profit and Loss Account and a Balance Sheet, in addition to the Government accounts.

q: The balances appearing under suspense heads in the subsidiary registers are periodically reconciled with:

options.A: The station balance sheets
options.B: The books of the Reserve Bank of India
options.C: The Appropriation Accounts
options.D: The General Books of the railway

e: The balances under suspense heads recorded in the subsidiary registers are periodically reconciled with the balances appearing in the General Books of the railway, to ensure the two agree.

q: The Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India on the accounts of the Union (including Railways) is submitted to:

options.A: The Railway Minister
options.B: The Chairman, Railway Board
options.C: The President of India, to be laid before Parliament
options.D: The Public Accounts Committee directly

e: The Report of the CAG on the accounts of the Union, including Railways, is submitted to the President of India, who causes it to be laid before Parliament.

q: Expenditure incurred in excess of the amount granted for a service in a financial year is regularised by Parliament by voting:

options.A: An Excess Grant
options.B: A Vote on Account
options.C: A token grant
options.D: A supplementary grant for the next year

e: Expenditure incurred in excess of the amount granted for a service in a year is regularised after the event by Parliament voting an Excess Grant for that service.

q: All revenues received and loans raised by the Government of India are credited, in the first instance, to:

options.A: Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: Public Account of India
options.C: Contingency Fund of India
options.D: Railway Development Fund

e: All revenues received by the Government of India and all loans raised by it are credited in the first instance to the Consolidated Fund of India.

q: The Contingency Fund of India, from which advances can be made to meet unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation by Parliament, is placed at the disposal of:

options.A: The Finance Minister
options.B: The President of India
options.C: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

e: The Contingency Fund of India is placed at the disposal of the President of India, so that advances can be made from it to meet unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation by Parliament.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Receipts such as Provident Fund deposits and departmental deposits are accounted for in the Public Account of India.
2. Disbursements from the Public Account of India require the vote of Parliament.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: Provident Fund deposits, departmental deposits and similar receipts are accounted for in the Public Account. Statement 2 is false: disbursements from the Public Account do not require the vote of Parliament, as Government holds these moneys as banker.

q: The earnings and receipts of Indian Railways form part of the receipts of the:

options.A: Public Account of India
options.B: Contingency Fund of India
options.C: Consolidated Fund of India
options.D: Railway Safety Fund

e: The earnings and receipts of Indian Railways are revenues of the Government of India and accordingly form part of the receipts of the Consolidated Fund of India.

q: The Annual Financial Statement of the Union Government is presented to Parliament under:

options.A: Article 110
options.B: Article 266
options.C: Article 267
options.D: Article 112

e: The Annual Financial Statement, the statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the Union Government for the year, is presented to Parliament under Article 112 of the Constitution.

q: A 'Vote on Account' enables the Lok Sabha to:

options.A: Vote a grant for an unexpected demand whose details cannot be stated
options.B: Make a grant in advance for a part of the financial year, pending completion of the regular budget procedure
options.C: Regularise expenditure incurred in excess of a grant
options.D: Vote the charged expenditure on the Consolidated Fund of India

e: A Vote on Account enables the Lok Sabha to make a grant in advance for a part of the financial year, so that Government can carry on until the regular budget procedure is completed.

q: A 'Vote of Credit' is granted by Parliament for meeting:

options.A: An unexpected demand upon the resources of India which, by reason of its magnitude or indefinite character, cannot be stated with the details ordinarily given in the Annual Financial Statement
options.B: The expenditure of the first four months of the financial year
options.C: Excess expenditure incurred in a previous year
options.D: A new service not contemplated in the Annual Financial Statement

e: A Vote of Credit is granted for meeting an unexpected demand on the resources of India which, by reason of its magnitude or indefinite character, cannot be stated with the details ordinarily given in the Annual Financial Statement.

q: If, during a financial year, the amount authorised for a service is found to be insufficient for the purposes of that year, the additional requirement is met through:

options.A: A Vote on Account
options.B: An Excess Grant
options.C: A Supplementary Grant
options.D: A Vote of Credit

e: When, during a financial year, the amount authorised for a service is found insufficient for that year, the additional requirement is met through a Supplementary Grant voted by Parliament.

q: A token grant is voted by Parliament in a case where:

options.A: The demand relates to charged expenditure
options.B: The Lok Sabha wishes to disapprove the policy underlying a demand
options.C: A grant is required for an unexpected emergency
options.D: The funds for a new service can be made available by re-appropriation within the existing grant

e: A token grant is voted where funds for a new service can be made available by re-appropriation within the existing grant; only a nominal sum is needed, but Parliament's approval for the new service is still taken.

q: A 'policy cut' motion in the Lok Sabha proposes that the amount of the demand be reduced to:

options.A: Re 1
options.B: Rs 100
options.C: Half the amount demanded

e: A policy cut motion proposes that the amount of the demand be reduced to Re 1, which signifies disapproval of the very policy underlying the demand.

q: A 'token cut' motion in the Lok Sabha proposes that the amount of the demand be reduced by:

options.A: Re 1
options.B: Rs 100

e: A token cut motion proposes that the amount of the demand be reduced by Rs 100, and is moved to ventilate a specific grievance within the sphere of responsibility of the Government.

q: In the Lok Sabha, the 'guillotine' is applied when:

options.A: A member is named by the Speaker for disorderly conduct
options.B: The Demands for Grants of a Ministry are passed without any discussion
options.C: On expiry of the time allotted for discussion of Demands for Grants, all outstanding Demands are put to vote together
options.D: The Appropriation Bill is introduced after the Demands are voted

e: The guillotine is applied when the time allotted for discussion of the Demands for Grants expires; all the outstanding demands are then put to vote together without further discussion.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Demands for Grants are voted only by the Lok Sabha.
2. The Rajya Sabha can also vote on Demands for Grants, though it cannot initiate them.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: Demands for Grants are voted only by the Lok Sabha. Statement 2 is false: the Rajya Sabha may discuss the Budget but it cannot vote on Demands for Grants at all.

q: The Estimates Committee of Parliament consists of:

options.A: 22 members drawn from both Houses
options.B: 15 members, all from the Lok Sabha
options.C: 45 members drawn from both Houses
options.D: 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha

e: The Estimates Committee consists of thirty members, all elected from the Lok Sabha; the Rajya Sabha has no representation on it.

q: The Public Accounts Committee consists of:

options.A: 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha
options.B: 22 members — 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha
options.C: 15 members, all from the Rajya Sabha
options.D: 25 members — 15 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha

e: The Public Accounts Committee consists of 22 members - 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha - elected by the two Houses by proportional representation.

q: The Chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee is:

options.A: Elected by the members of the Committee from amongst themselves
options.B: The Minister of Finance, ex-officio
options.C: Appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha from amongst the members of the Committee
options.D: Nominated by the President of India

e: The Chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha from amongst the members of the Committee; by convention, the post is held by a member of the Opposition.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Minister is not eligible to be a member of the Public Accounts Committee.
2. Members of the Public Accounts Committee are drawn from both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: a Minister is not eligible to be a member of the Public Accounts Committee, and the Committee's members are drawn from both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha.

q: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is often described as the 'friend, philosopher and guide' of:

options.A: The Public Accounts Committee
options.B: The Estimates Committee
options.C: The Railway Convention Committee
options.D: The Committee on Public Undertakings

e: The CAG assists the Public Accounts Committee with expert advice in its examination of the accounts and audit reports, and is therefore described as the friend, philosopher and guide of the Committee.

q: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is appointed by:

options.A: The President on the recommendation of the Public Accounts Committee
options.B: The President of India
options.C: The Prime Minister in consultation with the Chief Justice of India
options.D: A resolution of both Houses of Parliament

e: Under Article 148 of the Constitution, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is appointed by the President of India by warrant under his hand and seal.

q: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India holds office for a term of:

options.A: Five years or up to the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier
options.B: Six years or up to the age of 60 years, whichever is earlier
options.C: Five years or up to the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier
options.D: Six years or up to the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier

e: Under the CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971, the Comptroller and Auditor General holds office for six years or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.

q: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India can be removed from office:

options.A: In the like manner and on the like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court
options.B: By the President on the recommendation of the Union Cabinet
options.C: By an order of the Supreme Court
options.D: By the President on an address from the Lok Sabha alone

e: Under Article 148, the CAG can be removed only in the like manner and on the like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court, that is, on proved misbehaviour or incapacity after an address by Parliament.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The salary of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. After ceasing to hold office, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is not eligible for any further office under the Government of India or under the Government of a State.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: the salary of the CAG is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, and after ceasing to hold office he is not eligible for any further office under the Government of India or under the Government of a State.

q: Under Article 150 of the Constitution, the accounts of the Union and of the States are kept in the form prescribed by:

options.A: The Finance Commission
options.B: The President, on the advice of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: Parliament by law
options.D: The Ministry of Finance

e: Under Article 150, the accounts of the Union and of the States are kept in the form prescribed by the President, on the advice of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.

q: On Indian Railways, the compilation of accounts is the responsibility of:

options.A: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.B: The Railway Board directly
options.C: The Principal Director of Audit
options.D: The Railway Accounts Department, headed by the FA&CAO on each Railway

e: On Indian Railways, the compilation of accounts is the responsibility of the Railway Accounts Department, which on each Railway is headed by the Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer (FA and CAO).

q: The results of audit conducted in a field unit or office are communicated to the executive in the first instance through an:

options.A: Audit Para
options.B: Draft Para
options.C: Appropriation Account
options.D: Inspection Report

e: The results of audit conducted in a field unit or office are communicated to the executive in the first instance through an Inspection Report, listing the objections noticed during the local audit.

q: Action Taken Notes, conveying the final stand of the Government on paras appearing in the Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, are furnished to:

options.A: The Estimates Committee
options.B: The Public Accounts Committee
options.C: The Railway Convention Committee
options.D: The Ministry of Finance

e: Action Taken Notes, conveying the final stand of the Government on paras appearing in the Report of the CAG, are furnished to the Public Accounts Committee, which follows up the audit findings.

q: Compliance audit, as conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, is primarily concerned with examining whether:

options.A: Programmes have achieved their intended outcomes
options.B: The financial statements present a true and fair view
options.C: Transactions conform to the applicable rules, regulations and sanctions of the competent authority
options.D: The organisational structure of the audited entity is optimum

e: Compliance audit is primarily concerned with examining whether transactions conform to the applicable rules, regulations and the sanctions of the competent authority.

q: 'Propriety audit' extends the audit scrutiny beyond formal regularity, to examine:

options.A: Only the arithmetical accuracy of the accounts
options.B: Only the classification of expenditure between heads of account
options.C: Only the correctness of stock balances
options.D: The wisdom, faithfulness and economy of expenditure, bringing wasteful expenditure to notice

e: Propriety audit extends scrutiny beyond formal regularity and examines the wisdom, faithfulness and economy of expenditure, bringing wasteful and avoidable expenditure to notice.

q: The audit conducted by the organisation of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is essentially based on:

options.A: Cent-per-cent check of all transactions
options.B: Check of one month's transactions in full every year
options.C: Check exercised by the executive staff themselves
options.D: Test checks of transactions selected according to audit plans

e: Audit by the CAG's organisation is essentially based on test checks: transactions selected according to audit plans are checked in detail, instead of a cent-per-cent check of all transactions.

q: Internal audit on a zonal Railway is carried out by:

options.A: The audit party of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India stationed on the Railway
options.B: The Accounts Department of the Railway itself
options.C: The Vigilance Directorate of the Railway Board
options.D: The Ministry of Finance

e: Internal audit on a zonal Railway is carried out by the Accounts Department of the Railway itself, as distinct from the statutory audit conducted by the CAG's audit party.

q: In railway accounts, 'pre-check' of a claim means:

options.A: Audit of the claim after the payment has been made
options.B: Check of the claim by the audit office before the accounts of the year are closed
options.C: Examination and scrutiny of the claim by the Accounts office before payment is made
options.D: Check exercised at the time of preparation of the Budget

e: Pre-check means the examination and scrutiny of a claim by the Accounts office before payment is made, so that defects are caught before money is paid out.

q: Indian Railways is best described as:

options.A: A statutory corporation
options.B: A government company
options.C: An autonomous board outside the Government
options.D: A departmental commercial undertaking of the Government of India

e: Indian Railways is a departmental commercial undertaking of the Government of India: it is run as a Government department but maintains commercial accounts; it is neither a statutory corporation nor a Government company.

q: A recognised criticism of the dual system of railway accounts, under which Government accounts and Commercial accounts are maintained side by side, is that it involves:

options.A: Duplication of accounting work and records
options.B: Absence of parliamentary control over railway expenditure
options.C: Absence of any audit of railway transactions
options.D: Exclusion of Railways from the Finance Accounts of the Union

e: Under the dual system, the same railway transactions are recorded both in the Government accounts and in the commercial accounts, which involves duplication of accounting work and records.

q: The separation of Railway finances from the general finances of the Government of India was recommended by:

options.A: The Railway Convention Committee
options.B: The Acworth Committee
options.C: The Kunzru Committee
options.D: The Estimates Committee

e: The separation of Railway finances from the general finances of the Government of India was recommended by the Acworth Committee, and separation took effect from 1924-25.

q: The Financial Commissioner (Railways) functions as:

options.A: The Chairman of the Railway Convention Committee
options.B: The head of the Railway Audit organisation
options.C: Ex-officio Secretary to the Government of India in the Ministry of Railways
options.D: The chief accounting authority of each zonal Railway

e: The Financial Commissioner (Railways) functions as ex-officio Secretary to the Government of India in the Ministry of Railways, besides heading the railway finance and accounts organisation at the Board level.

q: The Depreciation Reserve Fund (DRF) on Railways is utilised primarily for financing:

options.A: Construction of new lines
options.B: Passenger amenity works
options.C: Staff welfare works
options.D: Renewals and replacements of existing assets

e: The Depreciation Reserve Fund is built up by appropriations from revenue and is utilised primarily for financing renewals and replacements of existing assets, not for creating new assets.

q: Works chargeable to the Development Fund (DF) on Railways broadly comprise:

options.A: Passenger and user amenities, labour welfare works and operational improvement works
options.B: Renewals of track and rolling stock
options.C: Doubling and gauge conversion works
options.D: Electrification of routes

e: Works chargeable to the Development Fund broadly comprise passenger and user amenities, labour welfare works and operational improvement works which are not chargeable to Capital or to the DRF.

q: The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh (RRSK), created in the Budget 2017-18 for safety-related works, had a corpus of:

options.A: Rs 17,000 crore over six years
options.B: Rs 1 lakh crore over five years
options.C: Rs 50,000 crore over ten years
options.D: Rs 20,000 crore over five years

e: The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh, created in the Budget 2017-18 for safety-related works, had a corpus of Rs 1 lakh crore over five years.

q: A zonal railway has gross traffic earnings of Rs 2,500 crore and gross working expenses of Rs 2,125 crore. Its Operating Ratio is:
e: Operating Ratio = Working expenses / Gross traffic earnings x 100 = Rs 2,125 crore / Rs 2,500 crore x 100 = 85 percent.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. For computing the Operating Ratio, working expenses include appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund.
2. The dividend payable to General Finances is treated as a part of working expenses for computing the Operating Ratio.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: for computing the Operating Ratio, working expenses include appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund. Statement 2 is false: dividend to General Finances is met out of surplus and is not a part of working expenses.

q: 'Capital-at-charge' of Indian Railways represents:

options.A: The book value of stores held in stock
options.B: The annual capital expenditure sanctioned in the Budget
options.C: The amount of dividend payable to General Finances
options.D: The total capital invested in the railway undertaking

e: Capital-at-charge represents the total capital invested in the railway undertaking, on which the Railways were expected to earn a return for General Finances.

q: The 'Block Account' in railway commercial accounts shows:

options.A: The details of wagons blocked at terminals
options.B: The suspense balances awaiting clearance
options.C: The grants blocked by Parliament during the year
options.D: The distribution of capital-at-charge among the various classes of assets

e: The Block Account shows the distribution of capital-at-charge among the various classes of assets, such as land, permanent way, bridges, buildings and rolling stock.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Appropriation Accounts of Railways are prepared by the Railway Accounts Department.
2. The Appropriation Accounts are certified by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India after audit.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: the Appropriation Accounts of Railways are prepared by the Railway Accounts Department, and they are certified by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India after audit.

q: The Finance Accounts of the Union Government present:

options.A: The accounts of the receipts and disbursements of the Government of India as a whole, including Railways
options.B: Only the grant-wise comparison of expenditure with the appropriations
options.C: Only the accounts of the Public Account
options.D: Only the debt position of the Government of India

e: The Finance Accounts present the accounts of the receipts and disbursements of the Government of India as a whole, including the transactions relating to Railways.

q: Savings anticipated in a grant during the course of a financial year should be:

options.A: Retained till the close of the year and surrendered thereafter
options.B: Surrendered as soon as they are foreseen, without waiting for the close of the year
options.C: Adjusted automatically against the grant of the next year
options.D: Kept under a suspense head till they are regularised

e: Savings anticipated in a grant during a financial year should be surrendered as soon as they are foreseen, without waiting for the close of the year, so that the funds can be used elsewhere.

q: Under Article 149 of the Constitution, the duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India in relation to the accounts of the Union and of the States are such as may be prescribed by:

options.A: Parliament, by law
options.B: The President of India, by order
options.C: The Ministry of Finance, through the General Financial Rules
options.D: The Public Accounts Committee

e: Under Article 149, the duties and powers of the CAG in relation to the accounts of the Union and of the States are such as may be prescribed by Parliament, by law.

q: The duties, powers and conditions of service of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India are laid down in:

options.A: The General Financial Rules, 2017
options.B: The Railways Act, 1989
options.C: The Comptroller and Auditor General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971
options.D: The Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules

e: The duties, powers and conditions of service of the CAG are laid down in the Comptroller and Auditor General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971.

q: Under the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971, the audit of all receipts which are payable into the Consolidated Fund of India is dealt with in:

options.A: Section 13
options.B: Section 16
options.C: Section 17
options.D: Section 20

e: Section 16 of the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 deals with the audit of all receipts which are payable into the Consolidated Fund of India.

q: The audit of the accounts of stores and stock kept in Government offices and departments is provided for in the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 under:

options.A: Section 13
options.B: Section 16
options.C: Section 19
options.D: Section 17

e: The audit of the accounts of stores and stock kept in Government offices and departments is provided for in Section 17 of the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971.

q: Unlike the corresponding authority in the United Kingdom, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India does NOT exercise the function of:

options.A: Controlling the issue of money out of the Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: Auditing the receipts of the Government
options.C: Auditing the accounts of stores and stock
options.D: Auditing Government companies

e: Unlike the corresponding authority in the United Kingdom, the CAG of India does not exercise the comptroller function of controlling the issue of money out of the Consolidated Fund of India; his role is audit only.

q: The audit findings of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India in respect of Railways are presented to Parliament through:

options.A: The annual report of the Railway Board
options.B: The Finance Accounts of the Union Government
options.C: A separate Audit Report of the CAG relating to Railways
options.D: The Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways

e: The audit findings of the CAG in respect of Railways are presented to Parliament through a separate Audit Report of the CAG relating to Railways.

q: The officers who man the audit organisation of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, including the Railway Audit offices, belong to:

options.A: The Indian Railway Accounts Service
options.B: The Indian Audit and Accounts Service
options.C: The Indian Civil Accounts Service
options.D: The Indian Defence Accounts Service

e: The officers who man the audit organisation of the CAG, including the Railway Audit offices, belong to the Indian Audit and Accounts Service.

q: 'Local audit' by the organisation of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India means audit conducted:

options.A: By the audited office's own staff
options.B: Only of local self-government institutions
options.C: Of the accounts of one selected month only, every year
options.D: At the premises of the audited unit by a visiting audit party

e: Local audit means audit conducted at the premises of the audited unit by a visiting audit party of the CAG's organisation, as opposed to audit done centrally.

q: Under the risk-based audit planning adopted by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, the frequency and intensity of audit of a unit are determined mainly by:

options.A: The assessed risk profile of the unit
options.B: The number of audit parties available
options.C: A fixed alphabetical rotation of units
options.D: The year of establishment of the unit

e: Under risk-based audit planning, the frequency and intensity of audit of a unit are determined mainly by its assessed risk profile: high-risk units are audited more often and more intensively.

q: An Internal Audit Charter of an organisation primarily defines:

options.A: The pay and allowances of internal auditors
options.B: The list of offices to be inspected each year
options.C: The purpose, authority and responsibility of the internal audit function
options.D: The format in which inspection reports are to be issued

e: An Internal Audit Charter primarily defines the purpose, authority and responsibility of the internal audit function within an organisation.

q: The Auditing Standards issued by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India are broadly aligned with:

options.A: The accounting standards of the ICAI only
options.B: The International Standards of Supreme Audit Institutions (ISSAI) of INTOSAI
options.C: The listing regulations of SEBI
options.D: The ISO 9001 quality standards

e: The Auditing Standards issued by the CAG of India are broadly aligned with the International Standards of Supreme Audit Institutions (ISSAI) issued by INTOSAI.

q: Before the Public Accounts Committee, the case of the Government on an audit paragraph is presented principally by:

options.A: The chief accounting authority (Secretary) of the Ministry concerned
options.B: The Comptroller and Auditor General himself
options.C: The Finance Minister
options.D: The officer who originally sanctioned the expenditure

e: Before the Public Accounts Committee, the case of the Government on an audit paragraph is presented principally by the chief accounting authority, that is the Secretary of the Ministry concerned.

q: Before Excess Grants are voted by Parliament, the excess expenditure reported in the accounts is first examined, and its regularisation recommended, by:

options.A: The Estimates Committee
options.B: The Railway Convention Committee
options.C: The Ministry of Finance
options.D: The Public Accounts Committee

e: Excess expenditure reported in the accounts is first examined by the Public Accounts Committee, and Excess Grants are voted by Parliament only after the Committee recommends regularisation of the excess.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Estimates Committee from the Public Accounts Committee?

options.A: The Estimates Committee examines accounts after the expenditure is incurred, while the Public Accounts Committee examines estimates before they are voted
options.B: Both committees examine expenditure only after it has been incurred
options.C: The Estimates Committee examines the estimates before expenditure is incurred and suggests economies, while the Public Accounts Committee examines expenditure after it has been incurred
options.D: The Estimates Committee is a joint committee of both Houses, while the Public Accounts Committee is not

e: The Estimates Committee examines the estimates before expenditure is incurred and suggests economies, while the Public Accounts Committee examines the expenditure after it has been incurred; the Estimates Committee is therefore prospective and the PAC retrospective.

q: An 'economy cut' motion in the Lok Sabha proposes that the amount of a Demand for Grant be reduced:

options.A: To Re 1
options.B: By a specified amount, representing the economy that can be effected in the expenditure
options.C: By Rs 100
options.D: To nil

e: An economy cut motion proposes that the amount of a Demand for Grant be reduced by a specified amount, representing the economy that can be effected in that expenditure.

q: Which of the following is 'charged' expenditure on the Consolidated Fund of India?

options.A: Salaries of the Members of the Railway Board
options.B: Payment of dividend to General Finances
options.C: Office expenses of the Railway Board
options.D: Sums required to satisfy a judgment, decree or award of a court against the Railways

e: Sums required to satisfy a judgment, decree or award of a court against the Railways are charged expenditure on the Consolidated Fund of India and are not submitted to the vote of Parliament.

q: In the Appropriation Accounts, the variation of actual expenditure, shown as excess or savings, is worked out with reference to:

options.A: The final grant or appropriation, after taking into account supplementary grants, re-appropriations and surrenders
options.B: The original budget grant only
options.C: The Revised Estimates of the year
options.D: The Budget Estimates of the following year

e: In the Appropriation Accounts, the variation of actual expenditure, as excess or savings, is worked out with reference to the final grant or appropriation, after taking into account supplementary grants, re-appropriations and surrenders.

q: Explanations for variations between the actual expenditure and the final grant are furnished in the Appropriation Accounts:

options.A: For every rupee of variation, however small
options.B: Only in the case of excesses over the grant
options.C: Where the variation exceeds the limits prescribed for the purpose
options.D: Only when specifically called for by the CAG

e: Explanations for variations between actual expenditure and the final grant are furnished in the Appropriation Accounts only where the variation exceeds the limits prescribed for the purpose.

q: The Finance Accounts of the Union Government are presented in two parts — Part I dealing with the Consolidated Fund of India and Part II dealing with:

options.A: Railways only
options.B: The Contingency Fund of India and the Public Account of India
options.C: The Defence Services
options.D: The accounts of the State Governments

e: The Finance Accounts are presented in two parts: Part I deals with the Consolidated Fund of India and Part II deals with the Contingency Fund of India and the Public Account of India.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Finance Accounts are compiled by the accounting authorities of the Government, and not by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
2. The Finance Accounts are certified by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India after audit.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: the Finance Accounts are compiled by the accounting authorities of the Government and not by the CAG, and they are certified by the CAG after audit.

q: Consequent upon the merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget, the payment of dividend by Railways to General Finances:

options.A: Has been dispensed with
options.B: Continues at the rate recommended by the Railway Convention Committee
options.C: Is made only in years in which Railways earn a surplus
options.D: Is now paid to the Contingency Fund of India

e: Consequent upon the merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget, the payment of dividend by Railways to General Finances has been dispensed with.

q: The 'Net Revenue' of a railway is arrived at by deducting from its gross traffic earnings:

options.A: The dividend payable to General Finances
options.B: The capital expenditure incurred during the year
options.C: Interest on market borrowings only
options.D: Working expenses, including appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund

e: Net Revenue is arrived at by deducting working expenses, including appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund, from gross traffic earnings; dividend was payable out of the surplus remaining after this.

q: The return on capital-at-charge of Indian Railways is computed as:

options.A: Gross earnings divided by working expenses
options.B: Net revenue expressed as a percentage of the capital-at-charge
options.C: Surplus expressed as a percentage of gross earnings
options.D: Working expenses expressed as a percentage of capital-at-charge

e: The return on capital-at-charge is computed as Net Revenue expressed as a percentage of the capital-at-charge, showing the rate of return earned on the capital invested in the undertaking.

q: The Performance Efficiency Index of a railway differs from its Operating Ratio in that the Performance Efficiency Index:

options.A: Is a purely financial ratio
options.B: Takes only goods traffic into account
options.C: Is a composite index built up from physical performance parameters relating to inputs and outputs
options.D: Is computed only at the Railway Board level for internal use

e: The Performance Efficiency Index is a composite index built up from physical performance parameters relating to inputs and outputs, whereas the Operating Ratio is a purely financial ratio.

q: The Committee on Public Undertakings does not examine the accounts and reports of Indian Railways because:

options.A: Railways is a departmental undertaking of the Government, and not a public undertaking in the form of a company or corporation
options.B: The accounts of Railways are treated as secret
options.C: Railways is audited by private firms of auditors
options.D: The Committee consists only of members of the Lok Sabha

e: The Committee on Public Undertakings does not examine Indian Railways because Railways is a departmental undertaking of the Government, and not a public undertaking in the form of a Government company or corporation.
